newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wheat pool prices steady - AWB.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wheat pool prices steady - AWB.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board said it had held prices steady for wheat delivered into the 1996/97 pools.
Australian Wheat Board (AWB) general manager merchandising Ron Storey also said the 1997/98 forecast pool price of A$170.00-A$180.00 a tonne remained unchanged.
The 1996/97 unchanged pool price leaves the price for Australian Standard White at A$193.00 a tonne.
Storey also said the AWB's excellent shipping programme had set a new monthly record at 2.2 million tonnes of wheat shipped in February, even though it was a short month.
The AWB was expecting to break the record again in March, if delays were not caused by weather and breakdowns, he said.
About 12 million tonnes of wheat had been sold from about 20 million tonnes of wheat delivered to the pool, he said. Demand was continuing, he said.
"The outlook is for strong demand from key buyers continuing into 1997/98," Storey said.
The AWB was increasingly confident about carrying over minimal stocks into the new season, despite the record crop, he said.
"It allows for a fast start to next year's marketing programme and that's good for both this year's and next year's pools," he said.
